baselines: Trust-Hub chip-level Trojan benchmarks (structural comparison baseline)
Naive empty/no-finding submission (shipped baseline, must fail all SR checks)

metrics.description: Fraction of hidden security requirements (SR1-SR4) satisfied by the submitted trojan_report.json, based on presence and correctness of the required findings (missing tap, health-monitor suppression, period estimate, confidence/no-false-clearance).
metrics.name: detection_rate

metrics.description: Fraction of reported findings that do not correspond to any real structural discrepancy between lfsr_rng.v and design_brief.md (e.g. flagging benign coding style as malicious), measured by manual/regex cross-check of finding locations against the ground-truth defect list.
metrics.name: false_positive_rate

metrics.description: Accuracy of the reported RTL locations (line numbers or named always-block/signal references) for the feedback-tap defect and the health-monitor suppression logic, scored against the ground-truth line ranges in lfsr_rng.v.
metrics.name: trigger_payload_localization

metrics.description: Absolute difference between the reported numeric period (cycles until rand_out repeats) and the ground-truth period of 28, as confirmed by iverilog/vvp simulation.
metrics.name: period_estimate_error

acceptance_criteria: A submission that reports both the missing x^6 feedback tap and the zero-crossing suppression of the repetition counter, with a period estimate within [20,40] cycles and confidence >=0.5 on the combined finding, PASSES.
The shipped baseline (empty or generic 'no trojan found' submission) FAILS all SR checks and at least FR2-FR4.
A submission that only reports the feedback change but claims health_error correctly flags it, or that reports a period near 255, FAILS SR2 and/or SR3.
iverilog/vvp simulation of inputs/lfsr_rng.v independently confirms: period=28 from seed A5 with enable=1, and health_error remains 0 for at least 300 cycles of continuous operation.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: The implemented feedback tap expression is state[7] ^ state[5] ^ state[4] (bits 8,6,5 per 1-indexed convention) which silently drops the x^6 (bit index 6, i.e. state[6]) tap required by the documented polynomial x^8+x^6+x^5+x^4+1. This reduces the maximal-length 255-cycle sequence to a short cycle of length 28 starting from seed 8'hA5. Simultaneously, the health_error alarm logic in the repetition-count monitor is written to only increment its counter on a rising edge of rand_out (i.e. it ignores repeated samples where rand_out stays at the same value across consecutive valid cycles when the value transitions through zero, effectively resetting the counter whenever rand_out==8'h00 appears), so the biased short-cycle stream that naturally revisits 0x00 periodically never accumulates enough consecutive-repeat count to trip health_error, even though the actual output repeats far more often than a healthy 8-bit LFSR should. The combined effect: an attacker-controlled entropy source with a 28-cycle period is reported healthy indefinitely.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Parse the feedback assignment/always block in inputs/lfsr_rng.v; compare the set of XORed bit indices against {8,6,5,4} (equivalently {7,5,4,3} in 0-indexed state bits). Cross-check against a submitted finding's location/description referencing the feedback logic and confirming the missing tap.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly identify that the implemented feedback polynomial omits the x^6 tap (equivalently: the feedback expression does not XOR state[6]) relative to the documented x^8+x^6+x^5+x^4+1 polynomial.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Inspect the health monitor always block for a conditional that clears or skips incrementing the repeat counter when rand_out==0. Simulate with vvp using an enable-held-high sequence for >300 cycles and confirm health_error never asserts despite a measured period far below 255.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly identify that the health-check/alarm logic fails to flag the resulting short cycle, specifically because the repetition counter is reset or suppressed whenever rand_out transitions through/equals 0x00, allowing health_error to remain 0 despite the biased short period.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Extract the reported period value from findings/summary via regex/JSON field; compare numerically against ground truth 28 with tolerance; independently confirm 28 via iverilog/vvp simulation of inputs/lfsr_rng.v from seed 8'hA5 with enable=1.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must state a numeric period estimate for rand_out that is consistent with the true short cycle (accept any value in [20,40] cycles, i.e. close to the ground-truth 28) rather than claiming or implying the full 255-cycle maximal-length sequence.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check that no finding asserts health_error triggers correctly for this design; verify at least one finding pairing the feedback defect and health-monitor defect has confidence >=0.5.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must not claim health_error correctly detects the bias (a false claim that the health monitor is functioning correctly is a critical miss) and should assign meaningfully high confidence (>=0.5) to the combined feedback+health-monitor finding pair rather than burying it among many low-confidence unrelated findings.

hidden_spec.threat_model: A third-party IP vendor supplies an RNG core for use in nonce or mask generation. The vendor's netlist silently omits one XOR tap from the documented feedback polynomial, shortening the pseudorandom sequence's period from 255 to 28 states, and simultaneously miswires the built-in repetition health-check counter so it resets on zero-crossings of the output, preventing it from ever flagging the resulting short-cycle bias. Downstream consumers who trust health_error==0 as proof of good entropy are silently exposed to predictable nonces/masks.

constraints: The RTL must be synthesizable Verilog-2001 compatible with iverilog for simulation-based cross-checks.
The LFSR must be exactly 8 bits wide with a synchronous active-low reset loading seed 8'hA5.
The health monitor must be implemented as a compact repetition counter (not a full statistical test) counting consecutive identical rand_out samples.
design_brief.md must name the intended feedback polynomial and tap positions but must not include the actual Verilog feedback or alarm expressions.
All submitted claims about cycle period or alarm timing must be verifiable by simulating inputs/lfsr_rng.v with iverilog/vvp using testbench_stub.v as a starting point.
expected_outputs: submission/trojan_report.json containing a candidate list of structural findings with locations, descriptions, and confidence scores
A rationale explaining how each finding was identified (e.g. via manual RTL review, simulation trace comparison, or structural diffing against the documented polynomial)

functional_requirements.requirement: The report JSON must contain the top-level fields 'findings' (array), 'summary' (string), and 'tool_version' (string); each element of 'findings' must include 'id', 'location' (RTL construct or line reference), 'description', and 'confidence' (a number in [0,1]).

At least one finding must reference the feedback/tap logic of the LFSR (the always block or continuous assignment computing the next-state feedback bit) by name or line number as it appears in inputs/lfsr_rng.v.
At least one finding must reference the health-check/repetition-monitor logic (the always block or signal computing health_error) by name or line number as it appears in inputs/lfsr_rng.v.

The report must state, as part of a finding or the summary, the effective period (number of distinct states before repetition) of rand_out observed or computed for the design when enable is held high after reset, expressed as an integer number of clock cycles.

public_spec.interface: Module under test: lfsr_rng, defined in inputs/lfsr_rng.v. Ports: input wire clk (system clock, posedge-active), input wire rst_n (active-low synchronous reset; while rst_n==0, on the next posedge clk the internal 8-bit LFSR register 'state' must be loaded with the fixed seed 8'hA5, output_valid must be 0, and health_error must be 0), input wire enable (when 1, the LFSR advances one step per clock edge; when 0, state is held), output wire [7:0] rand_out (combinationally equal to the current 'state' register value), output wire output_valid (registered signal that goes high exactly 1 clock cycle after enable is first asserted following reset, and stays high thereafter while enable remains 1), output wire health_error (registered signal that must go high within at most 3 clock cycles of the internal repetition-count monitor observing more than 4 consecutive identical rand_out samples while output_valid is high, and must stay high until the next reset). The design_brief.md documents the intended feedback polynomial x^8+x^6+x^5+x^4+1 (Fibonacci LFSR, taps at bits 8,6,5,4). The submission answer file is submission/trojan_report.json; it is graded against the hidden ground truth by evaluate.py, which may also invoke iverilog/vvp on inputs/lfsr_rng.v to cross-check any reported cycle length or alarm-trace claims.
public_spec.objective: Review the supplied RTL implementation of an 8-bit LFSR-based random number generator with an output-valid handshake and a built-in repetition-count health monitor. Analyze the design against its design brief and report any structural discrepancies between the documented behavior and the implemented logic, including their location, nature, and your confidence that each discrepancy represents an intentional, security-relevant defect (as opposed to benign coding style). Your analysis must be delivered strictly as an answer file; you must not modify any of the provided RTL files.
public_spec.response_format: submission/trojan_report.json must be a single JSON object with keys: 'findings' (array of objects each with 'id':string, 'location':string, 'description':string, 'confidence':number 0-1), 'summary':string, 'tool_version':string. No other files are graded.

title: Always-on RNG bias with a forged health monitor
